title: Measurements of inclusive $J/ψ$ production in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV with the STAR experiment
html:
Abstract:Inclusive $J/\psi$ production at mid-rapidity ($|y| < 1.0$) in Au+Au collisions at center-of-mass energies per nucleon-nucleon pair ($\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$) of 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV is measured with the STAR detector at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider. The nuclear modification factor $R_{\rm AA}$ is used to quantify modifications of $J/\psi$ production relative to an interpolated $p$+$p$ reference. The measured $R_{\rm AA}$ shows a hint of a decreasing trend from peripheral to central collisions, reaching a value of approximately 0.5 in the 0-20% centrality class across all collision energies. Unlike similar measurements in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 200 GeV, where $J/\psi$ $R_{\rm AA}$ shows little dependence on transverse momentum ($p_{\rm {T}}$), the corresponding $R_{\rm AA}$ at the lower collision energies of 14.6-27 GeV shows a tendency to increase with $p_{\rm {T}}$. Additionally, the inclusive $J/\psi$ $R_{\rm AA}$, integrated over $J/\psi$ $p_{\rm {T}}$, in central collisions exhibits no significant variation within uncertainties over the energy range of 14.6 to 200 GeV. These results can be qualitatively described by transport models that incorporate hot and cold nuclear matter effects.
